canonical_identity.title: Small Business Regulatory Reduction Act of 2025

plain_language_description: Would require the Small Business Administration to offset the estimated compliance costs of its new rules so its annual net regulatory cost to small businesses is zero or less.
prior_policy_baseline: CBO says agencies already publish analyses of significant small-business compliance costs and SBA already reports those costs. The new bill would add a statutory SBA-wide zero-or-below annual target and broader annual reporting.
proposed_action_or_mechanism: Beginning in FY2026, SBA would keep its small-business regulatory budget at zero or below, counting costs from issuing, modifying, or repealing rules. The Office of Advocacy would report federal-agency rule costs annually.
directly_affected: Small businesses affected by SBA rules

material_scale.deadline: FY2026 and each fiscal year thereafter

implementation_authority: SBA Administrator; Chief Counsel for Advocacy for reporting.
legislative_history: Passed the House on December 3, 2025; referred to the Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship on December 4; not enacted as of retrieval.

documented_supporter_rationale.summary: The House committee majority described the bill as limiting new regulatory burden and codifying a deregulatory cost-control approach.

documented_opponent_rationale.note: No concise opponent rationale is promoted into the dossier until a specific committee-minority or floor statement is reviewed claim by claim.

important_uncertainties: A zero-or-below accounting target does not establish which future rules would be issued, modified, delayed, or repealed.
CBO's implementation estimate is not an estimate of compliance savings or broader economic effects.
